test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II ( JSO ) 2021 Official Paper ( Held On: 10 August 2022 )
subject: general
question: Which is not relative measures of skewness?
solution:
The correct answer is __**mean - mode**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• Relative measures of **skewness **aim to quantify the degree of asymmetry in a given dataset with respect to some reference point.
 
• The first three options, ((Q3-Q2)-(Q2-Q1))/(Q3-Q1), ((P90-2P50)+P10)/(P90-P10), and ((D9-2D5)+D1)/(D9-D1), are all measures of skewness based on quantiles. They quantify the asymmetry of a dataset by comparing the difference between its median (Q2, P50, D5) and its extremes (Q1, Q3, P10, P90, D1, D9).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"MEAN- MODE" **is simply the difference between the mean and mode of a dataset and does not provide any information about the degree of asymmetry.
 
• The measure "Mean - Mode" is not considered as a relative measure of skewness because it is not expressed in terms of standard deviations, quartiles or other standard measurements.
 
• Skewness is the measure of asymmetry of a probability distribution and relative measures of skewness are expressed in terms of the standard units of measurement.
